summary: Verified UBOS Sub-pass B micro-patch: mime-icon endpoint Cache-Control/ETag/304 revalidation at both origin (localhost:8001) and through public ingress (Cloudflare). All 7 new tests + 23 regression tests pass (30/30). Discovered and fixed one critical bug: Cloudflare re-gzips the SVG and downgrades the strong ETag `"..."` to a weak `W/"..."` tag; browsers echo the weak form back on revalidation but the origin's exact-string If-None-Match match failed → returned 200 instead of 304 through the ingress. Applied RFC 7232 §2.3.2 weak comparison in /app/backend/routes/media.py. Now 304 works end-to-end through Cloudflare.
critical_code_review_comments: media.py mime_icon initially used exact-string If-None-Match matching (`etag in [t.strip() for t in inm.split(',')]`). This is not RFC 7232 compliant — the RFC mandates weak comparison for If-None-Match. Because Cloudflare (and Fastly/Akamai) re-encode payloads and downgrade strong ETags to weak, exact-string matching silently breaks 304 revalidation through any real CDN. Fixed with a `_normalize_etag` helper that strips optional `W/` prefix from both sides before comparing, and also handles the `*` wildcard case.

context_for_next_testing_agent: The mime-icon endpoint is fully verified at both origin and ingress. Origin: Cache-Control public/max-age=86400/immutable + CDN-Cache-Control (mirrored) + strong md5 ETag + Last-Modified + Vary: Accept-Encoding. Ingress (Cloudflare): Cache-Control gets rewritten to no-store/no-cache/must-revalidate (env-level, unavoidable), strong ETag gets downgraded to W/"..." (Cloudflare re-gzips), but ETag+Last-Modified pass through and 304 revalidation works. All 9 family shortcuts produce distinct ETags. Unknown family (e.g. 'wibble') falls back to generic icon with 200 + valid SVG.
rca of the issue:
Bug: Through Cloudflare ingress, If-None-Match: W/"<hash>" returned 200 instead of 304, breaking browser cache revalidation.
Root cause: Cloudflare re-gzips response bodies (Content-Encoding: gzip → applied by Cloudflare), which transforms the origin's strong ETag `"<hash>"` into a weak ETag `W/"<hash>"` (per RFC 7232, any content-coding transformation invalidates strong validators). Browsers on subsequent visits echo the weak form back in If-None-Match. The origin's original check did `etag in [t.strip() for t in inm.split(',')]` — an exact string match — so `"<hash>"` was not found in `[W/"<hash>"]`, and the endpoint fell through to returning a full 200.
Reproduction: curl -sD- -H 'If-None-Match: W/"<md5>"' https://<ingress>/api/media/mime-icon/pdf → HTTP/2 200 (before fix); HTTP/2 304 (after fix).
Fix: Added `_normalize_etag` that strips optional `W/` prefix from both the request's If-None-Match tags and the response ETag before comparing (RFC 7232 §2.3.2 weak comparison). Also accept `*` wildcard. File: /app/backend/routes/media.py, lines 257-275.
